title: Annotatio IV §.XXIV: rebuttal (2)–(3) — Trelcatius true text; REAL not CORPORAL; sacramental-spiritual mode vs local/gross
pass_a_gloss: Also (2) not all things are read in the Authors which the most Famous Man hints stand in them — for example in Trelcatius: ‘that Christ’s body is present on earth neither in a local nor an illocal mode’ does not stand there, seeing that Trelcatius’s words sound thus: For since Christ’s body, homoousion with ours, is in Heaven wherever it wills circumsriptively (namely from the nature of a body, which in a place — i.e. another body — cannot be present otherwise than circumsriptively), not by an invisible uncircumscribed mode (whether absolutely and simply such, or infinite — which is God’s alone — or indefinite / definitive, the essential habit Scholastics give angels) — which modes one and all overturn the truth of a body (as proper and essential adequately either to GOD or to Angels) — it must altogether be confessed that Christ is corporally in Heaven, yet with His Body present in the Supper in a sacramental, i.e. spiritual, mode. pp. 185–186. Also (3) whatever some Authors hand down of intentional or effective presence of Christ’s Body in the Supper; or others of a distance of Christ’s Body from the Supper no less than that between Heaven and earth; or a part of the very absence of Christ’s Body from the Supper; or finally Trelcatius of the circumsriptive mode of Christ’s Body’s presence affirmed in the heavens and the uncircumsriptive mode of being present denied on earth — all that they want opposed only to the corporal, local, and gross mode of Christ’s Body being present in or with or under the Eucharistic bread. For, says Trelcatius: Christ is truly present in the hearts of those who believe, with altogether the same presence as the Communion of His Body is exhibited to them in the Supper. And this presence is REAL, yet neither presence is CORPORAL. For by faith, as Ambrose says, Christ is touched, not by the Body. Leiden ed. p. 184 mid. And a few words later: The mode of the presence of Christ’s Body in the Supper is not CORPORAL, NATURAL OR LOCAL — whether by conversion of the whole substance of bread and wine into the Lord’s Body and Blood; or by IMPANATION or LOCAL INCLUSION; or finally by INEXISTENCE or indistancy, namely Corporal and Local — but is SACRAMENTAL and SPIRITUAL, which God’s will and Authority declared in the Institution words effects (p. 185 beg.). Otherwise the said Authors would with whole mind subscribe to every Real, Spiritual, Supernatural and Heavenly Presence and Exhibition of Christ’s true and substantial Body.
pass_b_english: Rebuttal (2): the alleged Trelcatius line ‘neither local nor illocal on earth’ is not there — Trelcatius says the body is circumsriptively in heaven yet present in the Supper sacramentally / spiritually (pp. 185–186).

Rebuttal (3): all that talk targets only corporal/local/gross presence in/with/under the bread. Trelcatius: the presence is REAL, not CORPORAL (Ambrose: touched by faith, not body); the mode is SACRAMENTAL and SPIRITUAL, not transubstantiation, impanation, or local inclusion — and those authors would subscribe every real spiritual supernatural celestial presence and exhibition.
source_text: Etiam (2) Non omnia in Autoribus leguntur quæ in iis exstare innuit Vir Clarissimus, exempli gratiâ, in Trelcatio: Nec locali, nec illocali modo corpus Christi in terra præsens esse, haud exstat, quandoquidem Trelcatii verba ita sonant; Cùm enim Christi corpus, nostro homoousion, in Cœlo, ubicunque vult, circumscriptivè sit, (puta ex natura corporis, quòd in loco, i.e. alio corpore, non potest aliter, quam circumscriptive adesse) non per modum invisibilem, incircumscriptum, (puta vel absolutè & simpliciter talem, seu infinitum (qui solius Dei est) vel indefinitum, (seu definitivum, Angelis à Scholasticis essentialem habitum) qui modi omnes & singuli veritatem corporis evertunt (utpote vel DEO, vel Angelis proprii & essentiales adæquatè) omnino Christum corporaliter in Cœlo, Corpore tamen in Cœna, modo sacramentali, i. e. spirituali, adesse fatendum est. pag. m. 185. 186.; Etiam (3) quicquid vel de intentionali, vel effectiva Corporis Christi in Cœna præsentia Auctorum nonnulli; vel alii de distantia Corporis Christi à Cœna, haud minori, quàm quæ Cœlum inter & terram obtinet; vel pars de ipsâ absentiâ Corporis Christi à Cœna; vel denique Trelcatius, de tàm affirmato circumscriptivo in cœlis Corporis Christi præsentiæ modo, quam negato incircumscriptivo in terris adessendi ejusdem modo, tradunt, id omne soli corporali, locali, crassóque Corporis Christi, vel in, vel cum, vel sub pane Eucharistiæ adessendi modo oppositum cupiunt: Nam, inquit Trelcatius; Cordibus eorum re verâ præsens Christus est, iis, qui credunt, eâdem omnino præsentiâ qualis & Communio Corporis sui ipsis exhibetur in Cœna. Atque hæc præsentia REALIS est, neutra tamen præsentia CORPORALIS. Nam fide, ut ait Ambrosius, tangitur Christus, non Corpore. Edit. Leidens. pag 184. in medio. Et paucis intersertis: Modus, ait, præsentiæ Corporis Christi in Cœna non CORPORALIS, NATURALIS AUT LOCALIS, sive per conversionem totius substantiæ panis & vini, in Corpus & Sanguinem Domini; sive per IMPANATIONEM aut INCLUSIONEM LOCALEM; sive denique per INEXISTENTIAM aut indistántiam, puta Corporalem & Localem: Sed SACRAMENTALIS & SPIRITUALIS est, quam efficit Dei voluntas & Auctoritas, verbis institutionis declarata: pag. 185. init. cæteroquin omni Reali, Spirituali, Supernaturali Cœlestique Corporis Christi veri & substantialis, tam Præsentiæ, quàm Exhibitioni, toto animo subscripturi Auctores dicti.
